subject: Re: Follow-up from Upperform and PG&E Support
why: Chuck rewrote your PG&E note to be less salesy and asked what you think. Salesmanship is the failure mode here.
inbound:
I made some suggestions. My key advice is to be more authentic and genuine. Subtly, it builds trust in people who are reading your words without the benefit of your body language and voice inflection. Also, I toned down the salesmanship a little. Take a look at let me know what you think:

------------------------------------------------
Subject: PG&E's Human Performance Journey

Dear Aaron,

I hope you had a chance to relax after our engaging conference in Seattle. On behalf of Upperform Partners, thank you for attending our presentation on Integrating Human Performance into Pigging Operations. I trust you found the session both valuable and insightful.

I got the sense from our interactions that your organization has made promising strides in integrating human performance tools and operational excellence into your business. That really piques my interest in learning more about your initiatives and discussing how Upperform Partners might contribute.

Could we arrange a brief team call to explore potential collaborations? A direct conversation would be the most effective way to exchange ideas and assess our opportunities for partnership.

I am flexible with timing and will accommodate your schedule. If preferred, you can include your admin in this correspondence to help find a suitable time.

Looking forward to our discussion and the possibility of working together.

Warm regards,

Yancey
reply:
Hey Chuck,

I agree completely. Your changes make it sound more like a real conversation and less like a pitch. That’s especially important here since Aaron only has the words in front of him.

I’ll use this direction and tighten up my outreach going forward.

Thanks,
Yancey
